areycruzer opened issue #102: Proposal: algo.RecallCert — certify a selection result against labels, in-engine
**Motivating consumer.** [substrate-friction](https://github.com/areycruzer/substrate-friction) measures whether graph-based test selection can reach labelled guarding tests (SWE-bench FAIL_TO_PASS as the oracle). Today the verdict is computed client-side: per-source bounded traversals (the dialect's outward-anchored variable-length form) at ~2 ms each, then set intersection and thresholding in the client. The same repo also computes an edge-set anti-join in-engine by reifying edges as nodes (see its `docs/engine-diff.md`) — the dialect already supports the traversal shapes; what is missing is a one-round-trip certification primitive.

**Proposal.** A procedure:

```
CALL algo.RecallCert(sourceNodes, labelNodes, relType, maxLen, threshold)
YIELD reached, total, recall, pass
```

Semantics: for each label node, is any source node within `maxLen` hops (directed)? `recall = reached/total`; `pass = recall >= threshold`.
